core.title: Place every test beneath its feature and test-kind directory
core.given: The plan models at least one wagon, feature or WMBT (plan artifact), and tests exist beneath the resolved test root (profile roots.test), outside vendored and generated trees.
core.when: You add, move or keep any test beneath the test root, or change the plan — existing tests are in scope too.
core.then: Every test beneath the test root lives beneath the directory of the feature it tests, in the subdirectory for the kind of test it is (the allowed shape from profile layout.feature_test_location).
prefer: Move the test beneath its feature, into the subdirectory for its kind of test, and give the test its URN and its acceptance binding.
avoid: Placing a test in a path that does not state both its feature and its kind of test.
Leaving a test without a URN naming its wagon, feature and acceptance and matching its path (mandatory companion obligation, enforced by its own rule).

Leaving a test without an acceptance binding, or binding an acceptance that does not exist or is not declared by a plan artifact (WMBT) that the test's own feature explicitly lists (mandatory companion obligation, enforced by its own rule).
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned (the stack-wide exclusion list, profile roots.excluded; the exact classification belongs to the checker).
core.why: A test proves an acceptance only when it names one that exists; its path says which feature and which kind of test it is.
evidence: The topology check, run over the whole resolved test root against the current plan, reports no path, URN or acceptance-binding finding.
The rule has a failing fixture demonstrating a misplaced or unbound test, as required of every rule in this set.
verification: Applies only when the plan models at least one wagon, feature or WMBT; then it covers every test beneath the resolved test root, not only changed files — including tests not yet assigned to a feature or to a valid directory. The plan is re-read on every run, so plan-only changes can create or invalidate violations.
Whole-tree check: each test's path is compared with the plan's wagons and features, independently of which files a change touched; pre-existing violations are findings.

Every test beneath the test root is in scope — of any test kind, however placed, and whether or not it is assigned to a feature. Which files beneath the root count as tests, and which kinds of test the stack distinguishes, is profile data (roles.assignment, layout.feature_test_location); a file beneath the root that is not a test is out of scope, not a violation.

Roots (config file, plan root, source root, test root, e2e root) come from the structure profile (roots.config, roots.plan, roots.source, roots.test, roots.e2e); defaults apply only when a key is not configured.

The allowed path shape is the profile's feature-and-test-kind test-location pattern (layout.feature_test_location), which governs every test beneath the test root; the check judges placement only, not test content.

The same check also enforces the companion obligations — the test's URN (profile urn.test) matching its wagon/feature path, and its acceptance binding (profile urn.binding.acceptance) declared by a plan artifact the test's own feature lists — and reports them as separate findings under their own rules.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned; the exclusion list is the stack-wide profile key (roots.excluded) and its exact classification is the checker's.
Severity 3, strict disposition: every finding fails.

values: plan models at least one wagon, feature or WMBT
test outside its feature and test-kind directory
test URN missing, or naming a different wagon/feature than the test's path
acceptance binding missing, acceptance unknown, or its declaring plan artifact not listed by the test's own feature

fires: The plan models at least one wagon, feature or WMBT, and any test beneath the resolved test root (configured or defaulted) — new, moved or pre-existing and untouched, of any kind and however placed — sits outside the allowed test location for its feature and kind of test.

The plan models at least one wagon, feature or WMBT, and a plan-only change (for example renaming or removing a feature) leaves an unchanged test beneath the test root in a path that no longer names a feature of its wagon.
(Companion rule) The plan models at least one wagon, feature or WMBT and a correctly placed test beneath the test root has no URN matching its wagon/feature path.

(Companion rule) The plan models at least one wagon, feature or WMBT and a correctly placed test beneath the test root has no acceptance binding, or binds an acceptance that does not exist or is declared only by a plan artifact the test's own feature does not list.
doesNotFire: The plan models no wagon, feature or WMBT yet.
Files inside vendored or generated trees, even beneath the test root.
Files outside the resolved test root (for example production source or end-to-end tests), including the default test tree when the test root is configured to a different directory.

proposedKeys.meaning: The allowed directory pattern for every test beneath the resolved test root: beneath the directory of the feature it tests, in the subdirectory for the kind of test it is (the kinds of test the stack distinguishes).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: layout.test_location covers only where a unit or acceptance test for a source file is placed. This rule needs the allowed placement of every test beneath the test root — explicitly including contract and integration tests and tests not yet assigned to a feature — keyed by feature and test kind. Narrowing to layout.test_location would weaken the all-tests scope, and layout.feature_dir / layout.wagon_dir name the plan-side code directories, not the test-kind subdirectories.

proposedKeys.meaning: The URN shape and declaration syntax by which a test names its own wagon, feature and acceptance (the test's identity header).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.<artifact> params cover component, acceptance, smoke_acceptance, train, wmbt, wagon, feature, journey — there is no test artifact; urn.binding.<artifact> binds a file to another artifact's URN, not to the test's own identity.

neutralityNotes: The scope is every test beneath the resolved test root — of any kind (unit, contract, integration, acceptance, whichever the stack distinguishes), however placed, assigned to a feature or not — preserved exactly from bun.json without assuming any role-union equivalence; test recognition is profile data (roles.assignment) and the allowed feature-and-test-kind directory pattern is profile data via the proposed key layout.feature_test_location, introduced because layout.test_location covers only the placement of a unit or acceptance test for a source file and would narrow the all-tests obligation. The core keeps exactly one obligation in then (placement) and retains the two mandatory companion obligations (test URN, acceptance binding) as avoid items, mirroring bun.json; their full split-rule realizations (atdd-bun.topology.test-urn-header and atdd-bun.topology.test-acceptance-binding, each with its own activation) remain Bun-side. 'wagon' and 'WMBT' are ATDD-method vocabulary already used by the profile vocabulary itself, so they are retained in the core. The exact vendored/generated exclusion list stays in the stack-wide profile key roots.excluded, with classification deferred to the checker. Two vocabulary keys were missing and are proposed: layout.feature_test_location (allowed feature-and-test-kind placement of every test beneath the test root) and urn.test (the test's own identity header). The path-glob activation fact has no neutral counterpart in the closed fact-type list, so it is folded into the file-kind fact plus profile-supplied scope.
